title.narrative: Enhancing resilience through the provision of lifesaving assistance Multi-Sectoral ( FSAC, WASH, Protection,and CCCM) to vulnerable IDPs, HCs, in Al Qahirah, Maqbanah, and Ash Shamayatayn districts.

description.narrative: ltpgtThis proposed 10-month project, contributing to YHF SA1 2025, aims to provide lifesaving assistance to vulnerable populations through multi-sectoral interventions, including CCCM, FSAC, and Protection in AlQahirah WASH, FSAC and Protection in Maqbanah and WASH in Ash Shamayatayn of Taiz. The project targets 18327 BNFs (4672 men, 4952 women, 4209 boys, 4494 girls) across 3 districts: 8804 (2243 men, 2381 women, 2017 boys, 2163 girls) in AlQahirah, 5,879 (1499 men, 1587 women, 1353 boys, 1440 girls) in Ash Shamayatayn, and 3644 (930 men, 984 women, 839 boys, 891 girls) in Maqbanah will benefit from one or more sectors under the project.ltbrgtIn CCCM, the project aims to enhance management and coordination of services at 16 sites in AlQahirah to improve living conditions of 1213 HHs (8804 persons: 2243 men, 2381 women, 2017 boys, 2163 girls). It also includes implementing site improvement to rehabilitate the damaged water network in Hawl Saddam School site (1019 BNFs) and fixing fire extinguishers at site level to enhance fire safety and protect people's lives and property.ltbrgtUnder FSAC, 372 vulnerable HHs in two districts will be provided with lifesaving emergency assistance. In AlQahirah, 312 vulnerable HHs (approx. 2184 persons: 428 men, 446 women, 642 boys, 668 girls) will receive emergency food assistance through Unconditional Cash Transfer (UCT) for six rounds to increase their access to safe and lifesaving food. In Maqbanah, 60 HHs (approx. 420 persons: 84 men, 90 women, 123 boys, 123 girls) will receive emergency livelihood assistance in terms of livestock kits (four small ruminants (goats), 150 Kg animal feed concentrate, and 15 Kg mineral blocks, UCT for 3 rounds), accompanied with nutrition-sensitive and livestock production practices awareness sessions.ltbrgtIn Protection, the project aims to support 3980 (1197 men, 1273 women, 746 boys, 764 girls) of the most vulnerable individuals from IDP, HC, and returnees (2066 in AlQahirah and 1914 in Maqbanah). Key activities include reactivating 2 CBPMs with 15 members, providing awareness-raising activities on protection for 1280 individuals, facilitating referrals for 200 individuals to services, conducting protection monitoring for 840 individuals, organizing structured recreational and PSS activities for 1215 children, providing multi-sectoral case management services to 150 at-risk children and supporting 180 vulnerable cases with cash for protection. Additionally, in Al Qahirah, the intervention provides multi-sectoral GBV case management services to 75 GBV cases and supports 25 GBV survivors with livelihood and skills-building services.ltbrgtIn WASH, the project seeks to ensure access to water, sanitation, and hygiene services for 9523 persons (2429 men, 2571women, 2192 boys, 2313 girls) from IDPs, HC, returnees, and Muhamasheen in critical sites and areas facing acute needs and disease risks in Maqbanah and Ash Shamayatayn. Key activities include extension of 3 water networks and constructing water points (1 in Wadi AlShat IDP site in Maqbanah and 2 in AlDuhrah and AlKadrah IDP sites of Ash Shamayatayn), serving 4211 persons. It will also involve distributing chlorine tablets to 1700 HHs. Besides, 8400 persons in the same districts will have support to safe sanitation and hygiene products and knowledge through constructing 102 emergency latrines (64 in Hojaij, AlHasbari, AlHajeb, Wadi Al Shat Sites, and Bane Hemiar in Maqbanah and 38 in AlKadarh and As Safyah sites in Ash Shamayatayn), serving about 612 persons providing in-kind HKs to 1500 HHs (450 in AlYemen and Hemiar of Maqbanah and 1050 in AlKadarah Site and 4 sites in As Safyah of Ash Shamayatayn) through WASH Cluster pipeline and training 8 CHVs to conduct HP in the same sites and areas, reaching out to 8400 persons.ltbrgtThe proposed project has been designed based on NA findings in FSAC, protection, and WASH sectors conducted by BCFHD in the targeted districts in Feb.-March 2025 and needs raised from the relevant authorities.ltbrgtlt/pgt
